core_obligations: Construct positive local boundary sections over the prescribed possibly singular orbit with slopes compatible with the Seifert gluing.
Choose alpha as a common multiple, calculate p,q,b and distribute fiber windings across connecting rectangles so all other solid tori can be capped by disjoint constant sections.
Show the resulting embedded interior is transverse and meets all orbits, and prove connectedness from the subgroup of Z/alpha generated by the winding increments.
Recover the exact regular-orbit intersection count and common positive boundary covering degree.

spans.label: local boundary-section construction with explicit form and transversality

proof_roadmap.step: The local contact model and slope inequality give embedded annuli positively covering the chosen boundary orbit.
Set alpha=lcm(alpha2,...), solve for p/q through the Seifert basis, and use e(Y)<0 for positive boundary degree.
Extend through connecting rectangles, attach alpha horizontal sections over the cut base, and cap the other solid tori along their meridians.
The winding shifts beta_i*alpha/alpha_i generate Z/alpha because their gcd with alpha is1; hence the constructed surface is connected.

difficulty_reason: After allowing the classical Seifert model, the task still requires a coordinated geometric construction: prescribed positive boundary covering, torus-basis changes, embedded gluing across a cut base, regular-fiber intersection control and a global monodromy/connectedness argument must hold simultaneously. This is not obtained by merely applying a surface-of-section theorem or the old fixed-point estimate. The constructive three-dimensional topology is beyond a routine qualifying-exam exercise, but no H3 is claimed. Independent review still required.

compared.difference: The new1089-1107 claim constructs a global section with all boundary components covering a prescribed Reeb orbit and specifies local slopes, intersection counts and covering degree; it is not the fixed-point estimate.

editorial_notes: Source1008 overstates uniqueness of the dual pair for(alpha,beta)=(1,0): determinant1 requires beta-prime=1, while alpha-prime is free. The displayed(0,1) is a valid choice used for the regular-orbit model. The original wording remains.
Source995 writes B_i when defining the j-th solid torus Y_j; surrounding993/997 and the subsequent gluing identify the disk as B_j. The original formula remains unchanged.

The auxiliary local setup1070 permits negative p_0, for which its later positive-intersection/orientation assertion is not valid in general. The counted theorem1092 and its construction1125/1131 explicitly require and produce p_0>0. Only this positive-cover branch is used and endorsed in the current problem; the printed broader auxiliary wording is retained and disclosed.

The coordinate projection(z,s)->z in995 is not the orbit quotient for the twisted circle action1025 when alpha_j-prime is nonzero. The classical Seifert orbit quotient is allowed as background, but those two maps must not be identified. The actual positive-cover proof uses the coordinate solid-torus neighborhoods, boundary bases, explicit action and horizontal caps; the exterior Y_0 has the genuine product projection. The original pi formulas are retained: no replacement pi or new gluing proof is inserted.

Panel(a) of the original figure labels the large cut base region with an intersection sign. The author explicitly defines B_0-prime in1157 as B_0 minus the connecting rectangles, and that cut region is used in the subsequent sheet construction. The original figure is retained.

source_issues.decision: For(alpha,beta)=(1,0), determinant1 forces beta-prime=1 but alpha-prime may be any integer. The asserted pair(0,1) is a permissible convention, not a uniquely forced pair. Choosing it supplies the regular orbit model used in the text; the main construction is valid with that choice. Preserve the original wording and disclose choice versus uniqueness.
Y_j is the solid torus B_j times S1; B_i in995 has a stray index, fixed by the surrounding j-indexed domain/codomain and subsequent formulas.

1070 permits p_0<0, but then the signed quantity -alpha_1*q_0-p_0*alpha_1-prime need not be positive under the written slope inequality. Examplealpha_1=1,alpha_1-prime=0,p_0=-1,q_0=1 gives-1. The counted theorem1092 and construction1125/1131 explicitly require and ensure p_0>0, where the local intersection and orientation statements are correct. Do not assert the unused negative branch.

The map(z,s)->z displayed995 is not invariant under the twisted circle action1025 when alpha_j-prime is nonzero, so it cannot literally be the orbit quotient asserted1034. The standard Seifert orbit coordinate is represented, up to disk reparametrization, by z^(alpha_j)*exp(2*pi*i*alpha_j-prime*s); its invariance follows directly from1025. The proof uses the coordinate solid torus, its boundary basis and that explicit action; over the free exterior Y_0 the projection really is(z,s)->z. Radial disks/solid-torus neighborhoods and constant-s caps used by the construction agree with the true orbit description. Preserve the printed formula but distinguish coordinate projection from the orbit quotient; no changed main theorem or new gluing argument is supplied.

Panel(a) displays an intersection sign in its large base-region label, while source1157 explicitly defines the cut region B_0-prime as B_0 minus the connecting rectangles. The geometric drawing and all later sheet gluing use the latter region. Retain original figure and mention the labeling slip if reproducing that panel.
